views.name: paper_author_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  writes.paperId AS paperId,
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  author.authorName AS authorName
FROM writes
JOIN author ON writes.authorId = author.authorId

params.description: Provides the association between papers and their authors, returning one row per (paperId, authorId) with the author's name.
params.when_to_use: List all authors for a given paper (e.g., show authors for paperId = X). | Find all papers authored by a given author (e.g., list paperIds for authorId = Y). | Compose higher-level queries that need a stable paper↔author link (e.g., count authors per paper, join paper-level metrics with author info). | Enrich paper-level results with author identity (e.g., display primary author names alongside paper records).
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper — derived from writes.paperId | authorId: identifier of the author — derived from author.authorId (via writes.authorId join) | authorName: display name of the author — derived from author.authorName
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- counts rows in this view; each row corresponds to one (paperId, authorId) association as produced by the base join | authors_per_paper(paperId) = COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId  -- can be computed on top of this view | papers_per_author(authorId) = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY authorId  -- can be computed on top of this view
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to a paper-level dimension or view on paperId — safe because this view is at one row per (paperId, authorId) and joining to a single-row-per-paper dimension will not duplicate the dimension's measures when the planner aggregates correctly (e.g., join paper table ON paper.paperId = paper_author_link.paperId). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to an author-level dimension or view on authorId — safe because this view is one row per (paperId, authorId) and joining to a single-row-per-author dimension will not duplicate the dimension's measures when aggregated correctly (e.g., join author table ON author.authorId = paper_author_link.authorId). | do NOT join to one-to-many tables/views (from paper_author_link's perspective) without re-aggregation first — for example, do not directly join to another writes-like table or another multi-author-per-paper view on paperId or authorId if that target contains multiple rows per the same key, because such joins can multiply rows and therefore duplicate counts/metrics derived from this view. | When composing metrics: if you need a paper-level metric (e.g., number of authors per paper) and you will join paper_author_link to another one-to-many table on paperId, first aggregate paper_author_link to one row per paper (e.g., COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId) to avoid duplication. | Similarly, if producing author-level aggregates and joining to multi-row author-related tables, first aggregate paper_author_link to one row per author (e.g., COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY authorId).

views.description: Provides the association between papers and their authors, returning one row per (paperId, authorId) with the author's name.

views.name: paper_authors_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(w.authorId) AS num_authors,
  GROUP_CONCAT(w.authorId) AS authors_concat
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregate of its authors: number of authors and a concatenated list of authorIds for each paper (one row per paper).
params.when_to_use: Get the count of authors for a specific paper or set of papers (e.g., how many authors wrote paper X). | List or display the authorId values associated with a paper (as a concatenated string). | Compose higher-level analytics that need one-row-per-paper author metrics (e.g., join paper-level author counts with citation counts, venues, or paper metadata). | Act as a pre-aggregated source to avoid re-counting authors when joining to one-row-per-paper dimensions.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the primary identifier of the paper (grouping key). | num_authors: COUNT(writes.authorId) — integer count of distinct rows in writes for the paper as produced by COUNT(w.authorId) in the view (note: COUNT of authorId here counts non-NULL authorId occurrences in writes). | authors_concat: GROUP_CONCAT(writes.authorId) — string that concatenates the writes.authorId values for the paper as produced by GROUP_CONCAT in the view (ordering and delimiter follow DB defaults).
params.metric: num_authors = COUNT(writes.authorId)  -- aggregate counting non-NULL writes.authorId rows per paperId as computed in the view query | authors_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(writes.authorId)  -- aggregation concatenating writes.authorId values per paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-paper dimensions (e.g., the base table paper or any other view that is 1 row per paperId) on paperId — safe because paper_authors_agg is one-row-per-paperId, so its measures (num_authors, authors_concat) will not be duplicated. | do NOT join directly to a one-to-many child of paper (for example, writes or any other table/view that has multiple rows per paperId) without first re-aggregating that child to one row per paperId — joining paper_authors_agg to such a many-side table will multiply the paper_authors_agg measures and produce inflated counts. | when combining with other many-sided aggregates: either (a) aggregate the many-sided table to the same grain (paperId) before joining, or (b) join at a higher grain with appropriate GROUP BY that re-aggregates measures (e.g., SUM(num_authors) after grouping by the desired grain) to avoid double-counting. | safe join example: JOIN paper_authors_agg pa ON pa.paperId = paper.paperId — safe because paper is one row per paperId and pa is one row per paperId. | unsafe join example: JOIN writes w ON pa.paperId = w.paperId — unsafe because writes is many-per-paper and would duplicate pa.num_authors and pa.authors_concat; if needed, first aggregate writes (e.g., counts or other metrics) to paperId before joining. | note on authors_concat: authors_concat is a derived string aggregation and will be duplicated or concatenated unexpectedly if the view is joined to many-side tables and not re-aggregated; treat it as atomic at the paperId grain and re-compute or aggregate appropriately when changing grain.

views.description: Per-paper aggregate of its authors: number of authors and a concatenated list of authorIds for each paper (one row per paper).

views.name: author_by_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  author.authorName AS authorName
FROM author

params.description: Provides one row per author (authorId) with the author's name; answers questions about authors and serves as a dimension to join author attributes onto aggregated measures.
params.when_to_use: Look up an author's name given authorId | Filter or group aggregated measures by author (e.g., papers per author) by joining this view as a dimension | Compose into larger queries that need author metadata (authorName) alongside aggregated metrics computed elsewhere
params.output_schema: authorId: the unique identifier of the author, derived directly from base column author.authorId | authorName: the human-readable name of the author, derived directly from base column author.authorName
params.metric: authorId = identity(author.authorId)  -- this view is at the grain of author.authorId (no aggregation) | authorName = identity(author.authorName)  -- attribute copied from base table
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to aggregations that are grouped by authorId (for example, join to paper_authors_agg on authorId) — safe because this view is exactly one row per authorId so joining does NOT duplicate aggregated measures that are already grouped by authorId. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or aggregate tables that use authorId as their grouping key (for example, any result that is one-row-per-authorId such as an aggregate of papers by author) on authorId — safe because both sides are one-row-per-authorId. | unsafe-to-join guidance: do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views (for example, paper_author_link) without first aggregating the many-side to authorId — joining author (one) to paper_author_link (many) will multiply author rows and therefore duplicate any measures taken from the author row if treated as metrics. Instead, if you need per-author counts or sums from paper_author_link, either (a) aggregate paper_author_link by authorId (e.g., COUNT(*) GROUP BY authorId) and then join, or (b) join and then group by authorId in the outer query to re-aggregate. | join examples (safe): join author_by_name AS a ON a.authorId = paper_authors_agg.authorId  -- safe: both are one-row-per-authorId | join examples (unsafe without re-agg): join author_by_name AS a ON a.authorId = paper_author_link.authorId  -- unsafe: paper_author_link is one-to-many and will duplicate author rows/measures unless you aggregate paper_author_link first

views.description: Provides one row per author (authorId) with the author's name; answers questions about authors and serves as a dimension to join author attributes onto aggregated measures.

views.name: paper_core
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COALESCE(p.year, NULL) AS year,
  COALESCE(p.numCitedBy, 0) AS numCitedBy
FROM paper p

params.description: Provides one-row-per-paper core attributes: paper identifier, publication year, and number of times the paper is cited.
params.when_to_use: Get basic paper-level facts (paperId, year, numCitedBy) for reporting or joining as a facts table. | Filter or group results by paper year or citation count. | Serve as the foundation (normalized grain = paper) to compose higher-level aggregates such as total citations by year or author when joined/aggregated correctly.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of a paper — derived directly from base table column paper.paperId | year: publication year of the paper (nullable) — derived directly from base table column paper.year; COALESCE(p.year, NULL) preserves nullability | numCitedBy: number of times this paper has been cited — derived from base table column paper.numCitedBy with COALESCE(p.numCitedBy, 0) to treat nulls as zero
params.metric: numCitedBy = COALESCE(paper.numCitedBy, 0)  -- base metric: per-paper citation count (no aggregation in this view) | year = COALESCE(paper.year, NULL)  -- preserved base attribute (nullable)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional/lookups that are one-row-per-key on paperId (or that are one-to-one with paper) — e.g., a hypothetical paper_details or paper_primary_source on paperId — safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paper, so measures (numCitedBy) are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to sibling selection views that return at most one row per paperId (e.g., author_by_name when filtered to a single author and then mapped 1:1 to a paper) only when uniqueness is guaranteed — safe because no multiplicative many-rows-per-paper will occur. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as paper_author_link (a join table linking papers to multiple authors) or paper_authors_agg if that view is many-rows-per-paper, without re-aggregation — joining paper_core to a many-rows-per-paper relation will multiply the paper_core row and thus over-count numCitedBy unless you re-aggregate afterwards (for example: sum(numCitedBy)/COUNT_DISTINCT(paperId) is not valid; instead, aggregate at paper level first or use DISTINCT paperId when aggregating). | recommended safe patterns when combining with one-to-many relations: | - To compute total citations by author: first join paper_author_link to paper_core at paperId and then aggregate citations per author using SUM(paper_core.numCitedBy) while grouping by authorId, ensuring paper_author_link has one row per (paperId, authorId). If author-paper is many-to-many and you want to avoid attributing full citation counts to each coauthor, choose an attribution method (e.g., fractional: SUM(paper_core.numCitedBy / paper_author_link.num_authors_for_paper)) after computing per-paper author counts. | - Alternatively, pre-aggregate paper_core at the paper grain (it already is) and then join only aggregated results into higher-level queries. | summary warning: because paper_core exposes a per-paper measure (numCitedBy) and is normalized to one row per paperId, any join that introduces multiple rows per paperId will duplicate that measure; always ensure joins preserve the 1:1 relationship or re-aggregate after the join.

views.description: Provides one-row-per-paper core attributes: paper identifier, publication year, and number of times the paper is cited.

views.body_sql:

       w.authorId AS authorId,
       a.authorName AS authorName
FROM writes w
JOIN author a ON a.authorId = w.authorId

params.description: Lists each (paperId, authorId) pairing and the author's name — i.e., which authors wrote which papers.
params.when_to_use: Retrieve all authors for each paper (one row per paper-author link). | Join author identity information (authorName) onto paper-centric queries at the paper-author grain. | Build aggregated metrics per paper or per author by composing/aggregating this view (e.g., count authors per paper, count papers per author) while preserving correct grain. | Serve as a canonical paper-author link when composing downstream joins that need author names.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of a paper; derived from writes.paperId | authorId: identifier of an author; derived from writes.authorId (and validated by author.authorId via the join) | authorName: name of the author; derived from author.authorName
params.metric: no measures are defined on this view; all output columns are base identifiers/attributes (no aggregates). If you need metrics, derive them in a separate aggregation step, for example: | paper_author_count_per_paper = COUNT(authorId) GROUP BY paperId | paper_count_per_author = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY authorId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core on paperId — safe because this view is at one row per (paperId, authorId) and paper_core is one-row-per-paper (paperId), so joining will attach paper attributes without duplicating paper-level measures (it will not multiply paper rows beyond the existing author links). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_by_name on authorId — safe because author_by_name is one-row-per-author (authorId), so it will not duplicate this view's rows or its derived aggregates. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views that expand either paperId or authorId (for example, a hypothetical paper_references table with multiple references per paper, or a paper_authors_agg-like view that lists multiple aggregated rows per paper) without re-aggregation, because joining a one-row-per-(paper,author) view to another one-to-many set on paperId will multiply rows and thereby multiply any counts or measures derived from this view. | If you need paper-level measures (e.g., count of authors) and then want to join other one-to-many detail (e.g., references), perform aggregation first: aggregate this view to paper-level (paperId, author_count = COUNT(authorId)) and then join the aggregated result to other one-row-per-paper dimensions or to one-to-many tables (if joining to one-to-many, ensure the aggregator is applied after the join or re-aggregate afterwards) to avoid double-counting. | Avoid joining this view to sibling join-views that also contain author links (e.g., another writes-based join) on paperId without disambiguating keys, because that can create many-to-many expansion; instead, join on the full key pair (paperId, authorId) when matching exact link rows.

views.name: paper_journal_publication
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paper.paperId AS paperId,
  paper.year AS year,
  paper.journalId AS journalId,
  journal.journalName AS journalName
FROM paper
JOIN journal ON paper.journalId = journal.journalId
WHERE paper.journalId IS NOT NULL

params.description: Provides one row per paper with its publication year and the journal it was published in (ID and name).
params.when_to_use: List papers with their publication year and journal name. | Filter or group papers by journal or year. | Join papers to journal-level metadata without causing duplication of paper-level rows. | Serve as a base for counting papers per journal or per year (when aggregated on paperId).
params.output_schema: paperId: the unique identifier of the paper, derived from table column paper.paperId | year: the publication year of the paper, derived from table column paper.year | journalId: the identifier of the journal in which the paper was published, derived from table column paper.journalId | journalName: the human-readable name of the journal, derived from table column journal.journalName
params.metric: row_count_papers = COUNT(paper.paperId) -- a paper-level count metric; compute by COUNT(paperId) after selecting from this view | distinct_journals = COUNT(DISTINCT journalId) -- journal cardinality in the result set | papers_per_journal = COUNT(paperId) GROUP BY journalId -- derive by aggregating this view on journalId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to journal (or journal-level dimension/views keyed by journalId) on journalId — safe because this view already joins paper -> journal 1:1 (each paper points to at most one journal) and the journal side is 1 row per journal, so measures aggregated at paper grain are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or any other paper-level normalized view) on paperId — safe because paperId is the grain of this view (one row per paper), so a join to another one-row-per-paper source will preserve row cardinality. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views such as paper_author_link or paper_author_link_4 without re-aggregation on the many-side (e.g., join only after aggregating authors per paper) because those joins will duplicate paper rows and thus multiply paper-level counts (papers_per_journal, row_count_papers). | do NOT join to paper_authors_agg unless you confirm its grain: if paper_authors_agg is aggregated to one row per paper (authors concatenated or counted), joining on paperId is safe; if it is one-to-many, re-aggregate first. | When composing metrics that depend on paper-level counts, always aggregate at the paper grain (paperId) after joining; for example, to get papers per journal, SELECT journalId, COUNT(paperId) FROM paper_journal_publication GROUP BY journalId. | If you need author-level metrics (e.g., papers per author), start from paper_author_link aggregated to one row per paper-author pair and aggregate appropriately, or aggregate paper_author_link to author-level before joining to this view to avoid duplication.

views.description: Provides one row per paper with its publication year and the journal it was published in (ID and name).

views.name: paper_authorship
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  w.paperId AS paperId,
  w.authorId AS authorId,
  a.authorName AS authorName,
  p.title AS title,
  p.year AS year,
  p.venueId AS venueId,
  p.journalId AS journalId
FROM writes w
JOIN author a ON a.authorId = w.authorId
JOIN paper p ON p.paperId = w.paperId

params.description: One row per (paperId, authorId) linking a paper to one of its authors with paper metadata and the author's name — useful for finding which authors wrote which papers and for answering co-authorship queries.
params.when_to_use: Find papers co-authored by specific authors (e.g., list paperIds that two named authors both appear on). | List all authors for a given paper along with paper metadata (title, year, venueId, journalId). | Filter papers by author attributes (e.g., authorName) while preserving per-paper metadata for downstream filtering or joins. | Compose queries that need the (paperId, authorId) grain as the base for deduplicated lists of paper-author pairs (e.g., distinct paper lists after author-level filtering). | Join to per-paper aggregates (that are one-row-per-paper) after filtering by author to produce per-paper results without duplicating rows (provided the join target is one-row-per-paper).
params.output_schema: paperId: paper identifier from writes.paperId (paperId) | authorId: author identifier from writes.authorId (authorId) | authorName: authorName from author.authorName (authorName) | title: paper title from paper.title (title) | year: publication year from paper.year (year) | venueId: venue identifier from paper.venueId (venueId) | journalId: journal identifier from paper.journalId (journalId)
params.grounded_columns: writes.paperId | writes.authorId | author.authorName | paper.title | paper.year | paper.venueId | paper.journalId
params.metric: No derived metrics are defined in this view; it surfaces raw columns at the (paperId, authorId) grain. Any derived per-paper or per-author metric must be computed with appropriate aggregation/deduplication outside or on top of this view.
params.composition: Safe: join this view to tables or views that are one-row-per-paper keyed on paperId (e.g., paper-level aggregates) — the join will preserve the (paperId, authorId) granularity without duplicating rows on the paper side. | Safe: join this view to tables or views that are one-row-per-author keyed on authorId (e.g., author-level aggregates) — the join will preserve the (paperId, authorId) granularity without duplicating rows on the author side. | Unsafe: do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables keyed on paperId (e.g., keyword or references tables with multiple rows per paperId) without first aggregating those tables to one row per paperId, because the (paperId, authorId) rows will be multiplied. | Unsafe: do NOT assume this view is one-row-per-paper or one-row-per-author. If you need paper-level outputs, deduplicate on paperId (e.g., SELECT DISTINCT paperId, title, year FROM paper_authorship) or aggregate appropriately; if you need author-level outputs, aggregate by authorId.
params.when_not_to_use: Do not use when you need true per-paper aggregates derived from one-to-many child tables (e.g., paper_keywords, paper_references) without first aggregating those children to one row per paperId — joining them directly will multiply rows because this view is at (paperId, authorId) grain. | Do not use when you need per-author aggregates that expect one-row-per-author unless you first aggregate the view up to authorId; directly treating this view as one-row-per-author will be incorrect because authors appear once per paper (wrong grain). | Do not use as-is to compute metrics that assume a single row per paper (paper-level cohort) when multiple authors per paper exist — this view will produce multiple rows per paper (one per author) and can produce inflated counts if not deduplicated. | Do not use if you need join paths or filters based on tables not referenced here (e.g., if a different join path to paper or author is required) because this view joins writes -> author and writes -> paper; alternative relationship paths are not represented.
params.dialect_notes: SQL dialect: SQLite. The SQL uses standard JOIN syntax and no dialect-specific functions.

views.name: paper_author_names_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS num_authors,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) AS author_names_concat
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
LEFT JOIN author a ON w.authorId = a.authorId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper aggregates of its authors: number of distinct authors and a distinct concatenation of their names, one row per paperId.
params.when_to_use: Get the count of distinct authors for a given paper or set of papers. | Show or filter papers by their author name list (as a concatenated string). | Compose with paper-level metadata (title, journal, year) without re-aggregating author measures. | Build further paper-level metrics that use the total number of authors as an input (e.g., authors per paper distributions).
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the primary key identifying the paper (grouping key). | num_authors: COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — the number of distinct authors who wrote the paper, derived from the writes.authorId column via COUNT(DISTINCT). | author_names_concat: GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName) — a concatenated string of the distinct authorName values for the paper, derived from author.authorName via GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT).
params.metric: num_authors = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId)  -- distinct count of authorId per paperId as computed in the view | author_names_concat = GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT author.authorName)  -- distinct concatenated authorName values per paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (NORM) on paperId — safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paperId, matching this view's grain (one row per paperId), so num_authors and author_names_concat are not duplicated. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_journal_publication (JOIN) on paperId — safe if that view is one-row-per-paperId (verify sibling view's grain); if it is one-row-per-paper, joining preserves measures. | do NOT join directly to writes (the writes table or any one-to-many view like paper_author_link) without re-aggregation — writes is many rows per paperId, so joining this aggregated view back to writes will multiply rows and therefore incorrectly duplicate num_authors and author_names_concat unless you re-aggregate after the join or join to a deduplicated/one-row-per-paper source. | do NOT join to any child table/view that is one-to-many from paperId (for example a table of citations, reviews, or multiple publications per paper) without re-aggregating — such joins will multiply this view's measures unless the consumer re-aggregates on paperId or joins on a one-to-one dimension. | safe composition pattern: if you need author-level details (authorId, authorName) alongside these aggregates, join to a de-duplicated author list per paper (e.g., a view that returns one row per paperId+authorId) and re-aggregate after any additional joins. For example: SELECT a.paperId, COUNT(DISTINCT a.authorId) AS num_authors, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT a.authorName) ... FROM (paper_author_link deduped) a GROUP BY a.paperId — do not rely on this aggregate view to be stable after joining to multi-author detail rows. | planner note: because this view groups at grain paperId and uses DISTINCT in its aggregates, any join that preserves the one-row-per-paperId cardinality (one-to-one) will not duplicate measures; any one-to-many join requires re-aggregation or joining to a pre-aggregated dimension keyed by paperId.

views.name: author_identity
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.authorId AS authorId,
  TRIM(a.authorName) AS authorName
FROM author a

params.description: Canonical author identity: one row per authorId with trimmed authorName; used to look up authorName by authorId or to join author-level name into queries.
params.when_to_use: Look up an author's canonical name given authorId (e.g., attach authorName when you already have authorId). | Join into queries that identify papers by author name only after resolving names to authorId (examples validated: finding paper IDs co-authored by two named authors where author names were resolved to authorId and then matched). | Composition into aggregations that are grouped by authorId (e.g., after computing per-author paper lists or counts) where exactly one row per authorId is required.
params.output_schema: authorId: author.authorId — canonical author identifier (grain of this view) | authorName: TRIM(author.authorName) — trimmed canonical author display name
params.metric: authorId = author.authorId | authorName = TRIM(author.authorName)
params.composition: Cardinality-safe: join to any fact or child table that references authorId when that side is the many-side (e.g., JOIN author_identity.authorId = paper_authorship.authorId). author_identity is one-row-per-authorId, so it will not duplicate itself; measures coming from the fact/child remain correct. | When combining with author-level aggregates, ensure the other side is aggregated to one row per authorId before joining (e.g., join to a subquery SELECT authorId, COUNT(*) AS paper_count FROM paper_authorship GROUP BY authorId). | Do NOT join author_identity to multi-row child tables and then treat author_identity-derived fields as aggregated without first aggregating/deduplicating the child side, because that will multiply author rows and distort counts or sums.
params.when_not_to_use: Do NOT use this view to deduplicate or resolve ambiguous names when you only have raw name strings and there may be multiple authorIds with the same trimmed authorName — the view keys on authorId, not authorName, so name-to-id disambiguation is not handled by this view. | Do NOT rely on this view to change row-level grain: it will not deduplicate or collapse multi-row child tables (wrong-grain risk). Joining author_identity directly to a many-rows-per-author fact (for example paper_authorship) without first aggregating the fact will multiply rows — the view does not prevent duplication of the fact-side rows. | Do NOT use this view to infer relationships that require joins through other tables (wrong join path) — the view only exposes authorId and trimmed authorName from table author; any relationship to papers or authorship must come from the appropriate linking tables (e.g., paper_authorship).
params.dialect_notes: SQLite: TRIM() is used to remove surrounding whitespace from authorName.

SELECT

params.metric: paper_dataset_pair = (paperId, datasetId)  -- the view is row-grained; no aggregates are defined in this view | count_distinct_datasets_per_paper = COUNT(DISTINCT datasetId)  -- example aggregate you can compute on top of this view (not materialized here) | count_distinct_papers_per_dataset = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId)  -- example aggregate you can compute on top of this view (not materialized here)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or paper_basic / paper_journal_publication) on paperId — safe because this view is one-row-per (paperId,datasetId) and joining on paperId to a one-row-per-paper dimension will not multiply dataset associations incorrectly when you only need to enrich each paper-dataset row with paper attributes. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any dataset dimension (if present) on datasetId — safe because the dataset dimension should be one-row-per-dataset, so measures at the paper-dataset grain remain one per association. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables/views keyed by paperId (for example a paper↔author link such as paper_author_link or paper_authorship) without re-aggregating first — joining to a paper->many authors table will multiply the rows for the same (paperId,datasetId) for each author, duplicating counts or sums computed on this view. | if you need author-level detail combined with these associations, either: (a) first aggregate the many-side to the paper level (e.g., authors_agg per paper) and then join on paperId, or (b) join and then re-aggregate to the desired grain (for example GROUP BY paperId, datasetId after the join) to avoid inflated metrics. | do NOT join to other multi-row aggregations that are not reduced to the same grain (paperId,datasetId) without re-aggregation — ensure the downstream planner either joins with a dimension that is one-row-per-key or performs appropriate aggregation (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT) on datasetId or paperId) after joining to one-to-many tables. | safe join example for counting datasets per paper: SELECT p.paperId, COUNT(DISTINCT d.datasetId) FROM paper_core p JOIN paper_dataset_associations d ON p.paperId = d.paperId GROUP BY p.paperId — this is safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paper and the aggregation is explicit. | unsafe join example: SELECT pda.paperId, COUNT(*) FROM paper_dataset_associations pda JOIN paper_author_link pal ON pda.paperId = pal.paperId GROUP BY pda.paperId — unsafe because joining to paper_author_link (many authors per paper) will multiply rows; remedy by aggregating authors first or using COUNT(DISTINCT pda.datasetId).

views.name: paper_dataset_agg
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pd.datasetId) AS dataset_count
FROM paper AS p
LEFT JOIN paperDataset AS pd ON p.paperId = pd.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: For each paper (paperId), how many distinct datasets are associated with that paper.
params.when_to_use: Count distinct datasets linked to a given paper (per-paper dataset counts). | Report dataset counts alongside other per-paper attributes (title, year, journal) when joined at paperId. | Filter or rank papers by number of associated datasets (e.g., top-N papers by dataset_count). | Compose higher-level metrics that aggregate dataset counts across sets of papers (e.g., total datasets across a collection, average datasets per paper) — but see composition rules.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the primary key identifying a paper (comes from table paper.paperId). | dataset_count: COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId) — the number of distinct datasetId values associated with the paper (derived from table paperDataset.datasetId via COUNT DISTINCT in the view SQL).
params.metric: dataset_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperDataset.datasetId) grouped by paper.paperId
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to any table or view that is one-row-per-paper (key = paperId) — e.g., paper_core, paper_basic, paper_authors_agg, paper_authors_agg_11 — on paperId — safe because this aggregated view has exactly one row per paperId, so joining on paperId will not duplicate dataset_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to normalized paper dimension or 1:1 per-paper views (paper_core, paper_basic, paper_journal_publication if it is 1:1) on paperId — safe for the same reason (one row per paperId in both sides). | DO NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or joins that produce multiple rows per paperId (for example: paperDataset (raw), paper_author_link, paper_authorship, paper_author_link_4, paper_authorship_9, or other JOIN sibling views that are many-to-many per paper) without re-aggregation: joining this view to a child table with multiple rows per paperId will cause duplication of dataset_count if you then sum or aggregate dataset_count across the result. If you need to combine dataset_count with data that is one-to-many per paper, either: | - re-aggregate after the join (e.g., SUM(dataset_count) over distinct paperId or compute AVG(dataset_count) by grouping on paperId), or | - join this view to a deduplicated/1:1 per-paper representation of the other data, or | - join the other table first and compute the dataset_count from paperDataset in the same query (i.e., push the COUNT(DISTINCT) into the composed query) to avoid mismatch. | When composing higher-level metrics: to compute totals across papers, aggregate dataset_count by SUM(dataset_count) over distinct paperId (the view is one row per paper, so SUM(dataset_count) is correct). Do not SUM(dataset_count) after joining to a many-row-per-paper table unless you first collapse that many-side to one row per paperId. | If you need to join on datasetId (e.g., to bring dataset metadata) join from paper_dataset_agg to a dataset-level table by expanding from paperId to paperDataset via a separate join to paperDataset de-duplicated to one row per (paperId,datasetId) or join to dataset table only after materializing the set of datasetIds for each paper; avoid joining directly to dataset-level tables that will create multiple rows per paper without re-aggregation.

views.description: For each paper (paperId), how many distinct datasets are associated with that paper.

views.name: author_id_by_name
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  author.authorId AS authorId,
  author.authorName AS authorName
FROM author

params.when_to_use: Resolve an author's display name when you only have authorId. | Join author metadata (name) onto author-level fact/aggregate queries. | Compose higher-level queries that need a deduplicated list of authors.
params.output_schema: authorId: the unique identifier for an author, derived from table author.authorId | authorName: the canonical/display name for the author, derived from table author.authorName
params.metric: authorId = author.authorId | authorName = author.authorName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author-level or many-to-one views/dimensions on authorId — safe because author_id_by_name is one-row-per-authorId so joining it to other tables keyed by authorId will not duplicate these rows. Example: join to author_identity on authorId if author_identity is also one-row-per-authorId. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables (e.g., paper_author_link, paper_authorship, paper_author_names_agg, paper_authors_agg, paper_author_link_4, paper_authorship_9) without re-aggregating or deduplicating first, because those tables contain multiple rows per authorId (one row per paper-author relationship or multiple name variants) and would multiply author-level rows/measures. | When composing measures that count authors, prefer to perform aggregation after joining (e.g., COUNT(DISTINCT author_id_by_name.authorId) or aggregate in the many-side table first) to avoid double counting. | Safe composition examples: | - Join to paper_core or paper_basic on paperId only when you first start from papers and then join in author_id_by_name through a deduplicated author key (e.g., derive distinct authorId per paper in an intermediate subquery). | - Join to author_by_name or author_identity on authorId if those sibling views are normalized to one row per authorId. | Unsafe composition examples: | - Directly joining author_id_by_name to paper_author_link on authorId in queries that assume one row per paper will create multiple rows per author (one per paper), so re-aggregation (GROUP BY) or DISTINCT is required to maintain correct author-level measures.

views.description: Provides a lookup of authors by id and their canonical name (one row per authorId).

views.name: paper_coauthor_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT w.authorId) AS total_authors,
  -- distinct_author_count_excluding_authorId: leave expression generic by computing counts per paper per excluded authorId via conditional aggregation;
  -- consumers can subtract (authorId IS ?) by joining with this view filtered by that authorId = X if needed.
  NULL AS distinct_author_count_excluding_authorId
FROM paper p
LEFT JOIN writes w ON p.paperId = w.paperId
GROUP BY p.paperId

params.description: Per-paper counts of authors: total number of authors listed on each paper and a placeholder for a per-paper count that excludes a given authorId (to be computed by consumers).
params.when_to_use: Get the total number of authors attached to each paper (one row per paperId). | Filter or join to paper-level metadata (title, journal, year) while preserving author-count as a paper-level metric. | Compose higher-level metrics that need authors-per-paper (e.g., average authors per paper across a subset of papers) without re-aggregating writes. | Compute per-paper author counts that will later be adjusted to exclude a specific author by joining a per-author exclusion detail and subtracting — the view supplies the base total_authors.
params.output_schema: paperId: paper.paperId — the PK/identifier for the paper; grain of this view is one row per paperId. | total_authors: COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) — number of distinct authorId values associated to this paper via writes; derived from writes.authorId aggregated per paper. | distinct_author_count_excluding_authorId: placeholder NULL in this view; consumers should compute (for a given excluded authorId = X) as total_authors - (CASE WHEN X is present on that paper THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) by joining to a per-paper-per-author presence indicator (e.g., a filtered version of the writes table or a sibling aggregated view that exposes per-paper-per-author existence).
params.metric: total_authors = COUNT(DISTINCT writes.authorId) grouped by paper.paperId | distinct_author_count_excluding_authorId = (not materialized here) suggested computation per paper for a specific excluded authorId X: total_authors - (CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM writes w2 WHERE w2.paperId = paperId AND w2.authorId = X) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END). This view leaves this column NULL; consumers must join or filter by authorId and adjust accordingly.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core (or paper_basic, paper_journal_publication) on paperId — safe because these are one-row-per-paper normalized views/tables, so joining preserves the one-row-per-paper grain and does NOT duplicate total_authors. | Safe to join to aggregated paper-level sibling views (paper_authors_agg, paper_authors_agg_11, paper_author_names_agg) on paperId because they are also one-row-per-paper aggregated outputs; measures remain at paper grain and will not be multiplied. | Do NOT directly join this view to writes (or any other one-to-many detail table such as paper_author_link, paper_authorship, paper_author_link_4, paper_authorship_9) without re-aggregation: those are one-to-many from paperId to rows, and joining them will multiply the paper-level row and therefore duplicate or inflate total_authors unless the planner re-aggregates back to paper grain. | If you need to combine this view with per-author detail (e.g., to calculate per-author share or to exclude an author), first derive a per-paper-per-author presence table (SELECT paperId, authorId, 1 AS present FROM writes GROUP BY paperId, authorId) or use a sibling JOIN view that is one-row-per-paper-per-author; then either (a) compute the exclusion boolean per paper and subtract from total_authors, or (b) re-aggregate after joining back to paper grain (GROUP BY paperId) to avoid duplication. | When composing for metrics like averages across papers, aggregate total_authors after joining filters: AVG(total_authors) over a filtered set of paperId rows is safe because the view is one-row-per-paper. | If joining to author-level normalized views (author_identity, author_by_name), join on authorId only when those joins are done against a per-paper-per-author relation (not directly to this AGG). Joining this AGG directly to author-level tables on authorId is semantically incorrect (different grain) and will either drop multiplicity or require re-aggregation.

views.description: Per-paper counts of authors: total number of authors listed on each paper and a placeholder for a per-paper count that excludes a given authorId (to be computed by consumers).

views.name: paper_basic_30
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId,
  p.title,
  p.venueId,
  p.journalId,
  p.year,
  p.numCiting,
  p.numCitedBy
FROM paper p

params.description: Base paper-level attributes and citation counts for each paper (one row per paper).
params.when_to_use: Look up basic metadata for a specific paper (title, venue, journal, year). | Build aggregated reports where the unit is paper (e.g., list top-cited papers, filter papers by year or venue). | Compose into larger queries that join paper attributes to dimensions (authors, venues, journals) while preserving correct counts. | Serve as the starting normalized relation when computing metrics per paper or rolling them up to higher-level entities after proper aggregation.
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier for the paper — derived from paper.paperId | title: paper title string — derived from paper.title | venueId: identifier of the venue (conference/collection) where the paper was published — derived from paper.venueId | journalId: identifier of the journal (if applicable) where the paper was published — derived from paper.journalId | year: publication year of the paper — derived from paper.year | numCiting: count of papers that cite this paper (a citation-incoming metric) — derived from paper.numCiting | numCitedBy: count of papers this paper cites (a citation-outgoing metric) — derived from paper.numCitedBy
params.grounded_columns: paper.paperId | paper.title | paper.venueId | paper.journalId | paper.year | paper.numCiting | paper.numCitedBy
params.metric: numCiting = base metric stored in paper.numCiting (pre-aggregated count of incoming citations per paper) | numCitedBy = base metric stored in paper.numCitedBy (pre-aggregated count of outgoing references per paper)
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to paper_core on paperId — safe because paper_core is one-row-per-paper (same grain) so joining preserves one row per paper and does not duplicate numCiting/numCitedBy. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to author_identity (or author_by_name) only via an aggregated authorship view (e.g., paper_authors_agg or paper_authors_agg_11) or to a paper_authorship relation that is known to be one-row-per-paper-per-author but followed by aggregation on paperId — safe if you re-aggregate after joining because these are one-to-many from paper to authors. | do NOT directly join this view to one-to-many tables/views such as paper_author_link, paper_authorship, paper_author_link_4, paper_authorship_9, or paper_journal_publication without re-aggregation. Those joins will multiply rows per paper (one-to-many) and thus duplicate numCiting/numCitedBy unless you either: |   - aggregate the joined result back to paperId (e.g., GROUP BY paperId and re-compute derived metrics appropriately), or |   - join using a distinct one-row-per-paper projection of the many-side (for example, pre-aggregate paper_author_link into a single authors list per paper via paper_authors_agg) before joining. | When rolling paper-level metrics up to higher grains (e.g., author, venue, journal), compute aggregated metrics from this view using appropriate aggregation functions: sum/avg/count on numCiting/numCitedBy as needed, taking care that numCiting/numCitedBy are already counts per paper (do not sum twice). | Joining to dimension/lookup views that are strictly one-to-one on venueId or journalId (e.g., a venue or journal dimension keyed by venueId/journalId) is safe because those are one-row-per-venue/journal and will not duplicate paper rows. | If you need author-level metrics derived from paper.numCiting, join paper_basic_30 to an authorship aggregation (paper_authors_agg or paper_authors_agg_11) that maps paperId to authorId with one row per (paper, author) and then aggregate by authorId carefully (e.g., SUM(numCiting) grouped by authorId) — this is correct only when you intend to allocate full paper counts to each author; if you need fractional allocation, apply appropriate weighting before aggregation.

views.description: Base paper-level attributes and citation counts for each paper (one row per paper).

views.name: paper_basic_31
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paper.paperId AS paperId,
  paper.title AS title,
  paper.year AS year,
  paper.venueId AS venueId,
  paper.journalId AS journalId
FROM paper

params.description: A normalized (one-row-per-paper) view that returns basic identifying metadata for each paper: id, title, year, venue id and journal id.
params.when_to_use: Fetch core metadata for a specific paper or set of papers by paperId | Serve as the base (grain = paperId) for analyses that need to join paper-level dimensions (authors, venues, journals) or to aggregate paper-level metrics | Compose into queries that count or aggregate papers by year, venue, or journal | Join to author, venue or journal lookup/detail tables when you need non-duplicated paper-level measures
params.output_schema: paperId: unique identifier of the paper — derived directly from paper.paperId (base column) | title: paper title — derived directly from paper.title (base column) | year: publication year of the paper — derived directly from paper.year (base column) | venueId: identifier of the venue (conference/workshop) where the paper appeared — derived directly from paper.venueId (base column) | journalId: identifier of the journal where the paper was published (if any) — derived directly from paper.journalId (base column)
params.metric: No derived aggregate metrics are defined in this view. All outputs are direct base columns (identity projection). | If you need a count metric, compute at paper grain, e.g. paper_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId) when aggregating from this view.
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimension/lookups that are one-row-per-key without re-aggregation — safe examples: |   - Join to a venue or journal dimension on venueId or journalId: JOIN venue_dim ON paper_basic_31.venueId = venue_dim.venueId — safe because paper_basic_31 is one-row-per paperId, and venue_dim is expected one-row-per-venueId, so paper-level measures will not be duplicated. |   - Join to a normalized paper_core (if also one-row-per-paperId) on paperId: JOIN paper_core ON paper_basic_31.paperId = paper_core.paperId — safe because both sides are 1:1 at paperId. |  | Do NOT directly join without care to one-to-many child tables/views that list multiple rows per paper (these will duplicate paper-level rows/measures) unless you re-aggregate the child side back to paperId first. Examples to avoid or guard against: |   - Do NOT join directly to paper_author_link, paper_authorship, paper_authorship_9, paper_author_link_4, or any author-link/join table on paperId, because those are many-to-one (many authors per paper) and will multiply rows. Instead, first aggregate authors to paper-level (for example, use paper_authors_agg or paper_author_names_agg which are aggregation views producing one row per paperId) and then join on paperId. |   - Do NOT join directly to paper_journal_publication or other publication join tables that have multiple rows per paper without re-aggregation. |  | Composition recipes: |   - To get paper-level author counts: join paper_basic_31 to paper_authors_agg (one-row-per-paperId aggregated metrics) on paperId — safe because paper_authors_agg is pre-aggregated to paperId. |   - To add author details without duplicating: join paper_basic_31 to author_identity (one-row-per-authorId) only after reducing author links to one row per paper (e.g., via an aggregated author list or a chosen primary author). |  | Rationale: paper_basic_31's grain is paperId (one row per paper). Any join that preserves a one-to-one or many-to-one relationship from the perspective of paper_basic_31 (paper -> single lookup row) will not duplicate paper-level measures. Any join that introduces multiple rows per paper must be re-aggregated to paperId before combining with this view to keep counts/metrics correct.

views.description: A normalized (one-row-per-paper) view that returns basic identifying metadata for each paper: id, title, year, venue id and journal id.

views.name: keyphrase_row
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  keyphrase.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId,
  keyphrase.keyphraseName AS keyphraseName
FROM keyphrase

params.description: A normalized lookup of keyphrase identifiers to their canonical keyphrase names; one row per keyphraseId.
params.when_to_use: When you need the canonical name for a keyphrase given its keyphraseId | When composing queries that attach keyphrase names to other entities (papers, authors, etc.) by keyphraseId | When building aggregates grouped by keyphrase and you need the keyphrase label (use this view as a dimension lookup)
params.output_schema: keyphraseId: unique identifier for the keyphrase (derived from keyphrase.keyphraseId) | keyphraseName: canonical name/text of the keyphrase (derived from keyphrase.keyphraseName)
params.metric: No derived metrics in this view; all outputs are base columns (identity projection): keyphraseId = keyphrase.keyphraseId, keyphraseName = keyphrase.keyphraseName
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to fact or child tables/views that reference keyphraseId (e.g., a hypothetical paper_keyphrase link table) on keyphraseId — safe because this view is one-row-per-keyphrase (normal form) so joining it does not duplicate keyphrase rows; the measures in the other side are preserved and keyphraseName simply annotates them. | do NOT join this view to a one-to-many child of keyphrase (if such exists) without handling multiplicity (for example, do not join directly to a table that stores multiple names/aliases per keyphrase) because that would multiply keyphrase rows and any keyphrase-level measures; instead pre-aggregate or deduplicate the many-side before joining. | When composing aggregates: if you GROUP BY keyphraseId (or keyphraseName) using measures from another table, perform the aggregation on that other table (or its aggregate view) first, then join to this view to add keyphraseName. This avoids duplicating measure counts/aggregates due to row-level joins. | Safe to join to normalized one-row-per-entity dimension views (e.g., other NORM sibling views like author_identity or paper_basic) on their respective keys because both sides are 1:1 per key and will not duplicate measures. | Unsafe without re-aggregation: joining to JOIN or AGG sibling views that represent one-to-many relationships (e.g., a paper_author_link JOIN that lists multiple authors per paper) could cause multiplicative duplication of measures if you expected one row per keyphrase; instead, use an aggregate of the many-side (paper_authors_agg or similar) or join via a pre-aggregated mapping.

views.description: A normalized lookup of keyphrase identifiers to their canonical keyphrase names; one row per keyphraseId.

views.name: paper_keyphrase_link
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  paperKeyphrase.paperId AS paperId,
  paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId
FROM paperKeyphrase

params.description: Provides the one-to-one links between papers and keyphrases (each row = one paper-keyphrase association).
params.when_to_use: List all keyphrases associated with a given paper (filter by paperId). | List all papers associated with a given keyphrase (filter by keyphraseId). | Filter or join papers by presence/absence of specific keyphrases before composing additional aggregations. | Serve as the linking table when counting distinct paper-keyphrase pairs or building paper-level keyphrase aggregates.
params.output_schema: paperId: identifier of the paper; derived from paperKeyphrase.paperId in the base table | keyphraseId: identifier of the keyphrase assigned to the paper; derived from paperKeyphrase.keyphraseId in the base table
params.metric: row_count = COUNT(*)  -- counts paper-keyphrase links (no additional aggregation present in this view) | distinct_papers = COUNT(DISTINCT paperId)  -- can be computed on this view to count unique papers linked to keyphrases | distinct_keyphrases = COUNT(DISTINCT keyphraseId)  -- can be computed on this view to count unique keyphrases
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to dimensional or one-row-per-paper views/tables (e.g., paper_core or paper_basic) on paperId — safe because paper_core/paper_basic are normalized to one row per paper, so joining will not duplicate the paper-keyphrase rows (the result will remain one row per paperId/keyphraseId link). | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to one-row-per-keyphrase dimension (if present) on keyphraseId — safe because a one-row-per-keyphrase dimension will not duplicate the links. | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables or views keyed by paperId (for example, a paper_authorship JOIN that has multiple author rows per paper) without re-aggregating or distinct-ifying first — such a join would multiply the paper-keyphrase link rows and thus duplicate any measures derived from this view (e.g., counting links or summing attributes). | do NOT join directly to one-to-many tables keyed by keyphraseId (if any) without aggregation — those joins will also multiply rows and inflate counts/measures derived from this view. | When you need to combine this view with a many-side relation (e.g., paper_authorship or paper_author_link), either: (a) aggregate the many-side to one row per paperId (or per keyphraseId) before joining, or (b) join and then re-aggregate the result at the intended grain (paperId,keyphraseId or paperId) to avoid double-counting. | Examples of safe composition in planner terms: JOIN paper_core ON paper_core.paperId = paper_keyphrase_link.paperId (no duplication); JOIN keyphrase_dimension ON keyphrase_dimension.keyphraseId = paper_keyphrase_link.keyphraseId (no duplication). | Examples of unsafe composition without re-aggregation: JOIN paper_author_link ON paper_author_link.paperId = paper_keyphrase_link.paperId (unsafe unless paper_author_link is first aggregated to one row per paperId).

views.description: Provides the one-to-one links between papers and keyphrases (each row = one paper-keyphrase association).

views.name: keyphrase_paper_counts
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  k.keyphraseId AS keyphraseId,
  COUNT(DISTINCT pk.paperId) AS paper_count
FROM keyphrase AS k
LEFT JOIN paperKeyphrase AS pk ON pk.keyphraseId = k.keyphraseId
GROUP BY k.keyphraseId

params.description: For each keyphrase (keyphraseId), how many distinct papers are associated with that keyphrase (paper_count).
params.when_to_use: Find the number of papers that mention or are tagged with a given keyphraseId. | Filter or rank keyphrases by their paper coverage (e.g., top keyphrases by paper count). | Compose with keyphrase metadata or other 1:1 dimensions to produce keyphrase-level reports. | As a pre-aggregated building block when computing rates or ratios per keyphrase (e.g., papers per author for keyphrases) — provided joins preserve cardinality or re-aggregation is done.
params.output_schema: keyphraseId: the identifier of the keyphrase; sourced from keyphrase.keyphraseId | paper_count: the count of distinct papers associated with that keyphrase; computed from paperKeyphrase.paperId with COUNT(DISTINCT)
params.metric: paper_count = COUNT(DISTINCT paperKeyphrase.paperId)  -- aggregated per keyphrase.keyphraseId as in the SQL
params.composition: cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to keyphrase (or any other keyphrase-level 1:1 view) on keyphraseId — safe because keyphrase_paper_counts has exactly one row per keyphraseId, so joining to another one-row-per-keyphrase table/view does NOT duplicate paper_count. | cardinality-SAFE join guidance: join to normalized keyphrase metadata/view (e.g., a keyphrase detail SEL/NORM) on keyphraseId — safe for enrichment without changing paper_count. | DO NOT join directly to paperKeyphrase, paper, or any other one-to-many table/view keyed by keyphraseId without re-aggregation, because those joins would multiply rows per keyphrase and therefore duplicate or inflate paper_count. If you must join to paper-level data, either: |   - join on keyphraseId and then re-aggregate (e.g., SUM or COUNT DISTINCT) to recompute metrics at the keyphrase grain, or |   - first reduce the paper-level data to one row per paperKeyphrase.paperId (or per paper per keyphrase) and then join. | When composing with other AGG sibling views (one-row-per-keyphrase) use standard joins on keyphraseId; when composing with views that are aggregated at different grains (e.g., paper-level aggregates, author-level aggregates, or paper-author join views), ensure you either align grains by aggregating to keyphraseId or use analytical expressions that account for the many-side multiplicity. | Examples of unsafe joins without re-aggregation: joining keyphrase_paper_counts to paper_author_link, paper_authorship, paper_core (paper-level), or any paper_* JOIN that produces multiple rows per keyphraseId — these will multiply paper_count unless you re-aggregate. | Examples of safe patterns: (1) keyphrase_paper_counts JOIN keyphrase_metadata ON keyphraseId; (2) keyphrase_paper_counts JOIN (SELECT keyphraseId, SUM(x) AS x FROM some_keyphrase_level_agg GROUP BY keyphraseId) ON keyphraseId.

views.description: For each keyphrase (keyphraseId), how many distinct papers are associated with that keyphrase (paper_count).

views.name: paper_citation_classification
views.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.paperId AS paperId,
  COALESCE(p.numCiting, 0) AS numCiting,
  COALESCE(p.numCitedBy, 0) AS numCitedBy,
  COALESCE(p.numCiting, 0) + COALESCE(p.numCitedBy, 0) AS total_citations,
  CASE
